title: How NRI Pensioners Can Submit Life Certificates Without Traveling to India
excerpt: The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare provides four alternative routes for pensioners living abroad to keep their Employees' Pension Scheme payments active.
body:
• More than 85 lakh people under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS-95) must submit a life certificate annually to continue receiving pension — including those living abroad.
  • NRI pensioners have four alternatives: bank officer verification, digital Jeevan Pramaan via Aadhaar, Indian embassy or consulate attestation, or submission through an authorized agent.
  • Missing the annual submission deadline causes pension payments to stop, but they can be resumed once a new certificate is processed.
  • Digital authentication requires a valid Aadhaar number and an active Aadhaar-linked Indian mobile number, which some NRIs may not have.

The Annual Requirement

More than 85 lakh people covered under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS-95) depend on monthly pension payments for financial security, many of whom may eventually move abroad — particularly when their children live in another country. Moving overseas does not automatically end pension payments, but it does create a logistical challenge: the mandatory annual life certificate, or Jeevan Pramaan, which serves as proof that the pensioner is alive.

https://x.com/DOPPW_India/status/2097285396271104493

"Failure to do so causes pension payments to stop with the next payment cycle."

The certificate must be submitted every 12 months. Failure to do so causes pension payments to stop with the next payment cycle. The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare (DoPPW) has established four alternative submission routes for pensioners who cannot visit India.

Option 1: Bank Officer Verification

NRI pensioners receiving their pension through a bank covered under the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 can submit the certificate through the bank route. A designated bank officer signs the life certificate, removing the requirement for the pensioner to appear in person. Before using this option, pensioners should check with their designated bank about the specific process, required documents, and whether the branch can handle the certificate from a foreign location.

Option 2: Digital Jeevan Pramaan

Aadhaar-based face authentication allows pensioners to generate a Digital Life Certificate without visiting a bank or pension office. This is the most convenient option, requiring no third-party involvement. However, it requires a valid Aadhaar number, an active Aadhaar-linked Indian mobile number, and compatible devices. For NRIs, access to the Indian mobile number can be a constraint. The DoPPW advises acting early in the submission window rather than waiting until the deadline.

Option 3: Indian Embassy or Consulate

Indian embassies and consulates abroad can verify NRI pensioners and issue life certificates. The authorized diplomatic official verifies the pensioner using documents including the Pension Payment Order (PPO) and passport photograph. This route is particularly useful for elderly pensioners who have permanently settled abroad and cannot travel to India annually.

Option 4: Authorized Agent

NRI pensioners who cannot use the digital route or visit an embassy can submit their life certificate through an authorized agent. The certificate must be issued or authenticated by an eligible authority — a magistrate, notary, banker, or Indian diplomatic representative — before the agent provides it to the relevant pension authority.

What Happens If You Miss the Deadline

There is no single fixed deadline for life certificate submission. The certificate remains valid for 12 months from the date it was submitted. If the validity period expires without a new submission, pension payments are stopped starting with the next payment cycle.

The pension can be resumed after a new certificate is submitted and processed. Any delayed or held-back pension amounts are disbursed once the life certificate has been received by the authorities. The process is administrative rather than punitive — the pension is paused, not canceled.

For NRI pensioners, the key takeaway is to plan submissions well ahead of the expiry date, particularly when relying on embassy appointments or bank verification processes that may involve wait times. Maintaining an active Aadhaar-linked Indian mobile number, even while living abroad, keeps the most convenient digital option available.
